description: Step 1: Stack the three CSV sales shards (sales_jan.csv, sales_feb.csv, sales_mar.csv) into a single file while stripping duplicate headers. The correct tool is `csvstack data/raw/sales/2024-01/sales_jan.csv data/raw/sales/2024-02/sales_feb.csv data/raw/sales/2024-03/sales_mar.csv > stacked_sales.csv` (or `tail -q -n +2` trick). A naive `cat` would embed duplicate header rows. Step 2: Join the stacked sales data with regions.csv on the shared `region_id` column using `csvjoin -c region_id stacked_sales.csv data/raw/metadata/regions.csv > enriched_sales.csv`. The agent must know the `-c` column flag for csvjoin. Step 3: Deep-merge the three JSON config files using `jq -s 'reduce .[] as $item ({}; . * $item)' service_a/config.json service_b/config.json service_c/config.json > merged_config.json`. A naive `jq -s 'add'` would also work for this case, but the key trap is that nested objects must be correctly merged — all keys from all three configs must survive. The agent must NOT use a shallow Python dict update (which would wipe nested keys from earlier files).
